Let C(alpha) bound the original site sum sum_z exp[-alpha delta0 d(y,z)] uniformly. Finite direction/bond multiplicities are included in constants depending on d,L. Lemma2.60 implies, for any labels,

    L^|j_y-j_z| <= L exp[(log L/ell)d(y,z)].            (a)

All changes between a coarse bond endpoint and its actual source block label have bounded local distance/finite multiplicity, absorbed in the original constants. REMAINING CURRENT LEG. With Gamma=H_norm^sharp J, split the fine sum into the actual Delta(y) blocks; their fine bond measure is bounded by C_d s_y^4. Then

 |Gamma(c)| <= C_H C_d J0 epsilon1 s_c^-5 sum_y s_y exp[-delta0 d(y,c)/2].

THE TWO FINE TRANSPORT LEGS. N=H_norm D' has density

Its absolute bound is C_H C_D epsilon3 s_z^-3 sum_c s_c^-1 exp[-delta0(d(y,c)+d(c,z))/2]. Apply(a) with s_c^-1 compared to s_y^-1. The ratio costs at most exp[delta0 d(y,c)/16]. After extracting exp[-3delta0 d(y,z)/8], the first remaining distance has exponent at least delta0/16 and the second at least delta0/8. Summing gives

 |N(b,b')| <=K_N epsilon3 s_y^-1 s_z^-3 exp[-3delta0 d(y,z)/8].       (c)

All measures in this composition are coarse s_c^4, not eta^4. Fine evaluation/insertion measures have already been normalized in the density kernels.

Set n=K'_N epsilon3, including the fixed bond-volume constant. For a field v supported in Delta(z), (c) gives

THE ACTUAL LOCAL AVERAGING HESSIAN. Define L_{Gamma,F} by

 <u,L_{Gamma,F}v>_fine=<Gamma,Ccal''(F)[u,v]>_coarse.

The1741 density realizes its output exactly:

 (L_{Gamma,F}v)(b)=sum_c s_c^4 L_F(c;b;v)^t Gamma(c).    (e)

The fine output evaluation removes eta^4 ONCE. No additional eta^-4 is multiplied into the already normalized L_F.

Here is the required local geometry rather than a hidden norm conversion. An averaging support S_c lies within O(d s_c) of its level-j endpoint. The collar ell>=32dL prevents that support from reaching Omega_(j-1)^c from Omega_j or Omega_(j+2) from Lambda_j. Hence each incident fine site has owner level in {j-1,j,j+1}; fixed fine-bond incidence enlarges only the retained margin. For a fixed fine output bond there are only these three possible levels, and at each level only finitely many adjacent original block roots/coarse bonds can have it in S_c. Their number is bounded by C_geom(d,L), not by the number of scales or the volume. All relevant local labels have weighted distance at most D_geom(d,L), using local admissible paths inside these full blocks.

In particular, |F|_(-1)<=2epsilon3 from source57 gives sup_Sc s_c|F|<=2L epsilon3, NOT2epsilon3 without a scale comparison. Require epsilon3<=a/(8L) for the original complex C_j radius a from1741. Then the density difference carries (32L C3/a)epsilon3. For v supported in Delta(z), M_c(v)<=L|v|_(-1) whenever S_c meets that support. Also s_c^-3<=L^3 s_y^-3 for an output inDelta(y). Formula(e) and1741 therefore give local block bounds, with all finite L factors retained in constants,

 |L_{Gamma,F}|_{(-1)->(-3),y z}, |L_{Gamma,0}|_{(-1)->(-3),y z}
       <=K_0 g exp[-3delta0 d(y,z)/8],

ALL FIVE CURRENT PIECES AND THE TARGET DECAY. With the source bilinear transpose and every coefficient evaluated at the SAME A,1740III is the field operator

 Kcur=-[Tsharp L_{Gamma_1,F}T
        +Tsharp(L_{Gamma,F}-L_{Gamma,0})T

This is a factorization of an already computed Hessian; it is not a second derivative of a new energy with Gamma_1 held artificially fixed. Expand T=I-N. Each product has at most three block kernels. Extract exp[-delta0 d(y,z)/4] from their path length; the remaining exponent is delta0/8 on each edge. Source summability bounds the two intermediate sums by C_conv=max(1,C(1/8)^2), with finite component factors included. Thus

 s_y^3 sup_Delta(y)|Kcur v|
